national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has emphasized that India must make geo-strategic thinking and contingency planning as integral parts of its preparedness amidst challenges arising from evolving technology, unpredictability, and geographical proximity. Addressing the Indian Navy Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi today, Mr Singh said that the country’s goal is clear that preparedness must reach the crisis point before the crisis itself reaches the doorstep. The Minister also underlined that the on-going ‘Operation Urja Suraksha’ has once again demonstrated the Indian Navy’s professionalism and operational readiness to protect the country’s energy supply lines and national interests. He added that India stands firm as the first responder, preferred security partner and as a symbol of trust and reliability in the Indian Ocean Region, strengthening the country’s vision of MAHASAGAR. The Defence Minister noted that the presence of Indian warships in South China Sea, Mediterranean, Atlantic Ocean, demonstrates the country’s blue-water force capability. The Defence Minister also commended the Indian Navy for maintaining a high level of combat readiness noting that it is acting as a strategic anchor in realizing India’s resolve of becoming a developed nation by 2047. He said India’s maritime power is aimed not merely at displaying the national flag at sea, but at ensuring that wherever the Tricolour is seen, it conveys security, trust and confidence. Deliberations during the conference included harnessing Artificial intelligence, Big Data, autonomous and uncrewed systems, cyber operations, logistics, training and technology absorption towards maintaining a Combat Ready – Credible – Cohesive – Future Ready force, guided by the principles of Jointness, Self-reliance, and Innovation.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 59 India rejects Turkish President Erdoğan’s unwarranted references to J&K at UNGA
national_raw_news.content: India has rejected the unwarranted references made by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on Jammu and Kashmir during his UNGA address. Briefing media in New Delhi today, External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that this is a matter pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty and no external party has any locus standi on the issue. On the IBSA statement, Mr Jaiswal noted that a meeting at the level of foreign ministers was held between India, Brazil and South Africa on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. He added that after the meeting, the three countries have come out with a joint statement wherein the collective view of the three countries has been put together. Mr Jaiswal pointed out that there are several economic issues, development issues, and certain political issues that have been reflected. He said India stands for a two-state solution, as far as its own point of view on Palestine is concerned. On the comments made by External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar on cross-border terrorism, Mr Jaiswal said External Affairs Minister highlighted that cross-border terrorism is a cause of major concern, and countries need to come together to fight this global menace. On the issue of a 100% tariff by the US, the spokesperson said that Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri had a meeting with the US Congressional delegation in New Delhi recently. He added that during the meeting, various issues of bilateral nature were discussed. Mr Jaiswal further noted that the Foreign Secretary conveyed concerns regarding the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SIRA) as to the kind of implications it would have for bilateral relationship as well as the international energy market. On Indian vessels in the Persian Gulf, the spokesperson informed that there are six India-flagged commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. He said there are six foreign-flagged vessels which are carrying cargo to India. He further said that there are around 163 Indian seafarers who are on board these vessels. Apart from this, there are over 4,500 Indian seafarers who are on board various commercial vessels which are operating in the area. Mr Jaiswal said that the Ministry of Shipping continues to monitor the movement of these ships and is looking at the well-being of all these seafarers. He expressed India’s commitment to the safety and well-being of the seafaring community abroad. Replying to a query on the India-Ganges Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh, Mr Jaiswal said India and Bangladesh have a joint river commission, and all matters relating to rivers will be discussed as part of this river commission. He added that at the technical level, meetings on the Ganga Water Treaty continue to happen.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 63 India clinches gold in Women’s 4×400m relay, Neeru Dhanda wins trap gold; Overall medal tally rea...
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian Games 2026, India today delivered a strong medal haul, adding eight medals, including two Gold, one Silver and five Bronze medals in relay, shooting, athletics and Boxing. India won the women’s 4 x 400 metre relay, clocking 3 minutes 29.69 seconds at Nagoya in Japan. India also bagged a Bronze in the men’s 4x400m relay and another Bronze in the mixed 4x100m relay. Earlier, Neeru Dhanda made history by becoming the first Indian shooter to win a gold medal in the women’s trap individual event in Japan. This was after she carried India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer. Gulveer Singh bagged bronze in the men’s 5000 metre final at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is Gulveer’s third medal of the Games after he clinched silver in both the men’s 10,000 metre and 1500m earlier in the competition. Pooja Singh also bagged Bronze in women’s high jump today. In Boxing, Narender Berwal won bronze in men’s boxing plus 90kg category after losing to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan by a unanimous 0-5 decision in the semi-final today. India has moved up to 10th place in the 2026 Asian Games standings, bringing its total medal tally to 53. The current tally includes 6 gold, 21 silver, and 26 bronze medals.

national_raw_news.title: Neeru Dhanda becomes first Indian shooter to win Asian Games gold in women’s trap 11 hours ago 241
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda has made history by becoming the first Indian shooter to win a gold medal in the women’s trap individual event. This came after she carried India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer. The Indian trio finished with a combined score of 328 points to secure the silver, finishing three points ahead of Kuwait, who took bronze with 325. China won the gold medal with a score of 346. In Boxing, Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal have stormed into the gold medal bouts of their respective weight categories with semifinal wins at Nishio today. Parveen defeated China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal, before Ankush came from behind to out-punch reigning 75kg world champion Uzbekistan’s Fazliddin Erkinboev 4-1 to book his place in the 80kg summit clash. In athletics, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s javelin throw. Yashvir Singh won the silver medal with a personal-best effort of 85.72 metres, while Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with a throw of 84.35 metres. In the men’s long jump, Sreeshankar Murali secured the silver medal with a best effort of 8.07 metres. Gulveer Singh also added another silver to his tally after finishing runner-up in the men’s 1,500 metres. He had earlier won silver in the men’s 10,000 metres. In shooting, Esha Singh won silver in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual event. The 21-year-old Indian shooter finished second with a score of 38 points. India has moved up to 11th place in the 2026 Asian Games standings, bringing its total medal tally to 47. The current tally includes 5 gold, 21 silver, and 21 bronze medals. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Trap Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that their precision and steady focus have brought this success. President Murmu has wished them to continue to keep their sights set on many more memorable achievements.

national_raw_news.title: Conservation is national responsibility, says Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav 57 mins ago 11
national_raw_news.content: Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav today said that conservation is not merely a government responsibility but is a national responsibility. Addressing the 4th Eco Warrior Awards and Eco Warrior Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Yadav said that forests are not just green patches on a map, but vital ecological infrastructure that support water systems, regulate climate, conserve soil, and sustain biodiversity and livelihoods. He highlighted that forest officers today face far more complex challenges than simply guarding boundaries, as they must manage landscapes while balancing conservation, development, and human aspirations. He also highlighted the growing threat of climate change, forest fires, habitat fragmentation, invasive species, and water stress, calling for a landscape approach that integrates forests, wildlife, agriculture, water, and communities. The Minister described the Forest Service as a service entrusted with the stewardship of India’s natural capital and acknowledged the contribution of frontline forest personnel. Mr Yadav said that their contribution must never be forgotten and that they are the people who convert conservation policy into conservation on the ground. He further said that the Eco Warrior Awards celebrate courage without publicity, service without applause and commitment without immediate rewards. He also recognised frontline forest personnel and stressed the role of tribal and forest-dependent communities as conservation partners. During the event, the Lifetime Achievement Award was presented to 1976-batch IFS officer Brij Kishore Singh for his contribution to forest and wildlife conservation, including efforts against sandalwood smuggling and Veerappan’s activities in Karnataka.
